title: Output spec
lead: Decide portrait or landscape, delivery resolution and frame rate first. The aspect sets the framing of every keyframe and video and locks once the first keyframe is adopted; changing it later means redoing generated keyframes and videos.
lockedTitle: The aspect locked at {{time}} when the first keyframe was adopted; changing it shows the impact first

platform.title: Where it will be published
platform.lead: A platform fills in the aspect and resolution below; you can still change them one by one.

note.9x16: Full-screen on a phone held upright; short-drama platforms everywhere are portrait-first. The main image and video models make 9:16 natively.
note.16x9: For landscape players like Bilibili and YouTube. On portrait short-drama apps it shows wide black bars.
note.3x4: Shorter than 9:16, so people and places fit more easily; full-screen playback leaves bars top and bottom.
note.1x1: Mostly for ads and social feeds.
note.21x9: Nano Banana Pro does not do 21:9: keyframes are made at 16:9 and then outpainted or cropped; H3's 2K tier is about 2976×1248 here.

impact.title: Changing to {{name}} affects work already done

res.title: Resolution and frame rate

desc.1080p: The usual ceiling on short-drama platforms; recommended. Finals come from the H3 API or a local upscale to this size.
desc.2k: Finals get an extra 2K finishing step: local SeedVR2 is free but slow; H3 2K regeneration is about $0.10 / s (output + input).

res.draft: Drafts always use the 768p tier ({{w}}×{{h}}) on local H3, free; finals are made at the delivery resolution once you adopt.

fpsNote.24: MiniMax H3 and the other video models output 24 fps natively; no conversion.
fpsNote.25: Converted from 24 to 25 fps at export; camera moves may stutter slightly. Only affects export, no video redo.
fpsNote.30: Interpolated to 30 fps locally at export (e.g. RIFE); takes longer and fast motion may show artefacts. Only affects export.

lenNote.short: At episode 1's pace (34 s, 9 shots, about 3.8 s each), about 8–24 shots per episode. Episode planning splits by this length.
lenNote.mid: About 24–47 shots per episode. Episode planning splits by this length.
lenNote.long: About 47–79 shots per episode; reviewing takes much longer.
lenNote.xl: About 160 shots per episode; run the pipeline on short episodes first.

compat.title: Can the models on the current route make this spec directly?
compat.note: Unsupported models are hidden in the pickers; vendors' docs are authoritative

how.native_4k: Renders at this aspect directly, up to 4K
how.outpaint_from_16_9: Make 16:9 first, then outpaint or crop to 21:9
how.upscale_from_1k: Some channels only reach 1K at this aspect; upscaled locally to the delivery size
how.h3_aspects: Six aspects from 21:9 to 9:16, 24 fps, 5–15 s per clip
how.follow_draft: Follows the draft's aspect; 2K tier short edge 1440
how.upscale_from_720p: Supports this aspect; some channels only reach 720p and need an upscale
how.any_aspect: Only enlarges, keeps the framing; any aspect

output.title: Audio, subtitles and export
output.deriveNote169: At export each shot is outpainted at the sides by AI, billed by the outpainting model; no video redo.
output.deriveNote916: At export each shot is cropped to portrait around the people, free; content at the edges is cut off.

preview.title: Framing and safe areas
preview.lead: The storyboard and keyframe pages overlay the same guides. Keep faces and key text out of where platform buttons and captions cover the picture.
preview.caption: {{name}} · {{w}}×{{h}} · {{fps}} fps
preview.ariaSub: , subtitles inside the lower safe area
